findings.finding: The 1.4475p Q2 interim dividend goes ex on 24 September 2026, the same session as the H1 results. That is 1.92% of the 75.35p sealed spot. The stage's resolver measures unadjusted Yahoo closes, and on this name's last ten clean ex-dates the raw close fell a median 1.58% (mean 1.19%, 8 of 10 negative).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raw close-to-close on this name's ex-dates from Yahoo's v8 chart with events=div: 2023-11-30 -4.22, 2024-03-14 -1.30, 2024-05-30 -1.86, 2024-09-19 -0.91, 2024-11-28 -1.29, 2025-03-27 +3.41 (three days after FY results), 2025-05-29 -2.25, 2025-09-18 +0.72, 2025-12-04 -1.89, 2026-04-02 -2.34. The 2026-07-09 row is dropped because Yahoo's data around it is corrupted (a pence/pounds error: 0.768).
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced, and it is not an information edge: the market will mark the dividend off at the open. It belongs in the number for a different reason. eu_resolve.py closes() reads q['close'] from Yahoo's v8 chart, which is not dividend-adjusted (the adjclose series differs from it on this very name). So the scored window close(23 Sep) to close(24 Sep) contains the dividend coming off, and the baseline does not see it: priced_lean is +0.075, and neither history nor event_move_proxy flags an ex-date. If this were already in the baseline, the lean would carry a -1 to -2 point ex-div component, or the resolver would read adjclose.
findings.independence: The ex-date comes from the issuer's RNS only. The drop size is backed independently by Yahoo's own dividend event series and raw closes on this name (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/LIVE.L?range=3y&interval=1d&events=div), and the unadjusted-close use by /home/user/claude_research/researcher_europe/scripts/eu_resolve.py (closes(), line ~365). The FY26 5.79p target made of four quarters of ~1.4475p is also in https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/living-reit-plc--live/dividend-guidance-declaration-new-debt-facility/9593290

outside_window.finding: The senior-living acquisition completed on 16 July 2026, after the H1 period end. Edison estimates the net assets acquired at a fair value of c GBP132m (including the mark-to-market on the 3.46% Scottish Widows debt) against GBP107.3m consideration. So IFRS NAV should take a gain in H2, while adjusted EPRA NTA is 'very slightly' diluted. At most it is a post-balance-sheet disclosure in these interims; the numbers land with FY26 results in March 2027, and Edison has already published the analysis.

Edison's FY26–28 forecasts carry a voluntary 5% haircut to SSH contracted rent for unforeseen tenant problems. Edison says that without it, earnings and dividend-paying capacity would be 7–8% higher. A clean H1 with no tenant problems would show this in the run-rate, but the haircut is in the published note and is really a full-year guidance item, not something this print settles.
